headline: Large Users Pay Grid Upgrade Costs
short_summary: This bill shifts the financial responsibility for dedicated electrical infrastructure from general ratepayers to large energy users like data centers, aiming to reduce residential utility bills.
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger, consumer advocates, environmental advocates, state lawmakers
opponents: Data center developers, large energy users
news_headline: Virginia orders data centers to pay for new transmission infrastructure
news_summary: The State Corporation Commission (SCC) has ordered that data centers and other large-load customers must pay for transmission infrastructure built exclusively to serve their facilities. This decision, supported by Governor Spanberger, aims to protect families and small businesses from hundreds of millions of dollars in transmission expenses previously spread across all utility customers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandate
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the volume of water delivered to data centers, increasing transparency on the industry's water consumption.
news_headline: Lawmakers negotiate data center water reporting bills
news_summary: Virginia lawmakers negotiated differences between Senate Bill 553 and House Bill 496, both aimed at addressing water use by data centers. SB 553, as originally proposed, would require water suppliers to report water delivered to data centers to the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, with the goal of increasing transparency on the industry's water consumption.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulations
short_summary: This bill mandates site assessments for new data centers to examine sound profiles near residential areas and schools, and allows localities to consider other environmental impacts during siting.
supporters: Local residents, environmental advocates, Delegate Josh Thomas
news_headline: Virginia, home to hundreds of data centers, adds new restrictions
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills to regulate data centers, including efforts to reduce noise and track water usage. These new restrictions respond to concerns from communities about the impact of massive data center structures on local resources and quality of life.
